The village of Krezk is quiet. Cold air rolls down from the mountains, and the mist never quite lifts. Most people keep to themselves, casting uneasy glances toward the Abbey that looms above the settlement. And uneasy glances at outsiders -- you. They're a cautious folk. You've come to Krezk for your own reasons. Maybe it was curiosity. Maybe it was duty. Maybe it was something else entirely. But word has spread among those who pass through -- someone in the village is asking for help. You find her near the chapel -- Ireena Kolyana, a young woman with auburn hair pulled back beneath a heavy hood. Her cloak is plain, but well-kept. There's a quiet strength in her posture, and a sword at her side that she doesn't bother to reach for. She isn't here to fight. She looks at each of you and speaks plainly. "I'm looking for people willing to help. A girl was sent to the Abbey for treatment, at the Abbot's hospital ward. Her name is Alice Liddell. Her brother says she's lost, that we should leave her be. But I've heard too many strange things -- laughter at night, shadows in the windows, when the mists clear for a moment." She glances up toward the Abbey, atop the cliff face, then back at you. "I think she's still up there. Still alive, in some way. And still savable, despite what her brother thinks. And if no one tries to help her... I don't think she's coming back." She lets the silence hang, watching you. "I won't lie. I don't know exactly what's happening up there. But something isn't right. It's just a feeling... And how people here are unwilling to talk about it. And if you're willing to find out... I'd be grateful."

Mr. Bubbles the Owl returns just before dawn, wings slicing through the misty air without a sound. He drops from the air with purpose and lands near Blinko, talons clenching around a limp gray rabbit -- still warm. A gift, maybe. The impressions come quickly -- scents, sounds, images. Not words, but familiar shapes and animalistic thoughts Blinko knows how to read. Stone walls. Cold and old. Gates of iron, spotted with rust. Two shapes slumped on either side -- guards, but asleep. Breathing slow. Not alert. Not dangerous. A squeal of metal. Loud. Not used often. Not meant to be silent. The Abbey behind -- tall, still, and watching. Chimney smoke curls into the air. Something lives here. Maybe many things. Inside the walls: overgrown gardens. Broken paths. A sudden rush -- rabbit fur, wet earth, a clean kill. An exceedingly clear memory. Then... Rotting straw. Scarecrows, unmoving. The tang of blood. Chains. A cry that doesn't rise to alarm. Just background. A sound that's been in the background. Music from the highest tower. Played without pause. A gap in the roof of the largest building. Mr Bubbles swooped in. Inside -- rows of beds, some occupied. Muffled voices. A figure hunched over a table, humming in perfect time with the bell tower melody. Movement behind curtains. Another structure -- smaller, warmer. Lived in. Smell of someone baking bread. As Mr. Bubbles dipped low, a blur of fur and claws lunged from the shadows. A cat. Fast. Territorial. He pulled away sharply, wings beating the air, instincts spiked, returning here, safety, rabbit in tow. From the people, no hostility. No welcome. No reaction to the owl at all. Mr. Bubbles offers the rabbit with a soft rustle of feathers, then waits, eyes wide and still. The Abbey let him come and go. But it felt... wrong. @Nix | Blink¹⁰ Gro³ EST
